case: Deterministic state preservation across script reload
requirement: Covered and baseline output/state agree, including state on an instance created before instrumentation reloads its script

obligations.note: autoload _ready(); same line, same count, regardless of the later reload(true) call -- the point of this case is that the reload does NOT re-trigger _ready() or otherwise disturb this obligation.

notes: Isolates gd-tools 0.4.0's own stated mechanism -- Script.reload(true) on an already-running autoload's script, called from coverage.gd's addon _ready() -- from its actual instrumentation step, which this fixture does not perform (the script's source is unchanged across the reload call). Result on the pinned Godot 4.7.1 build: reload(true) preserves both object identity (same_instance=true) and mutated instance-variable state (counter carries 11 into the reload and reaches 111 afterward, matching the no-reload baseline exactly) with reload_err=0. This is a real, engine-version-specific finding, not an assumption: it means the reload mechanism itself is sound on this engine build, so if a future real-adapter run finds gd-tools mishandling state, the defect is in the instrumentation step itself or in something reload(true) does NOT preserve (e.g. running scripts with active coroutines, or non-Node RefCounted instances, which this fixture does not exercise), not in reload(true) itself. This case's real evidence (final counter values, reload_err, same_instance) is not fully expressible as line-hit obligations -- the trivial single obligation above (line 10, always hit once) is included for schema consistency, but the actual finding lives in the per-input fields (expected_final_counter, expected_reload_err, expected_same_instance) and measured_on_engine, not in a hit/miss comparison.
author: godot-tooling-session-2026-09-19
reviewer: independent review agent (fable), 2026-09-19: re-ran driver_baseline.gd and driver_covered.gd on the pinned engine, confirmed reload_err=0/same_instance=true/counter=111 for both; found and flagged this file's and driver_covered.gd's stale 'gd-tools rewrites the file on disk before reloading' claim, already retracted in F040.json's correction but not yet propagated here -- corrected in this pass.
ambiguities: Only tested on a Node-based autoload with plain instance variables. A RefCounted instance holding a live coroutine (interacts with F045/F046) or a Resource with exported properties are separate, unbuilt variants.

Does not test reload(true) when the in-memory source has actually changed (gd-tools' real use case: it assigns instrumented GDScript text to the script's source_code property, then calls reload(true) -- not a disk rewrite, per F040.json's correction). This fixture only shows the reload mechanism preserves state when the source is unchanged; a changed-source variant belongs with a real adapter run.
